interpretations: For each `(orderslink, acctscope)` pair with a nonmissing average fee rate, calculate its excess over the global mean of all pair averages; retain positive excesses and return the three highest-excess pairs per scope, assigning a distinct rank to each pair
For each qualifying pair, calculate the same excess and use standard competition ranks within its scope; return every pair ranked 1, 2, or 3, including ties
For each qualifying pair, calculate the same excess and use dense ranks within its scope; return every pair in the three highest distinct excess levels, including ties
queries:
WITH pair_averages AS (
    SELECT f.orderslink, u.acctscope, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_fee_rate
    FROM fees AS f
    JOIN orders AS o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink
    JOIN users AS u ON u.userstamp = o.userlink
    GROUP BY f.orderslink, u.acctscope
    HAVING AVG(f.feerate) IS NOT NULL
),
excesses AS (
    SELECT orderslink, acctscope,
           avg_fee_rate - (SELECT AVG(avg_fee_rate) FROM pair_averages) AS excess
    FROM pair_averages
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT orderslink, acctscope, excess,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY acctscope
               ORDER BY excess DESC, orderslink
           ) AS rank
    FROM excesses
    WHERE excess > 0
)
SELECT orderslink, acctscope, excess, rank
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 3
